ECOSUSI Vintage Canvas Sport Tote Gym Bag Overnight Shoulder Bag Weekend Travel Duffel Bag Khaki [[VIDEOID:aed816f7c2aaf0d164823759a497b104]] [[VIDEOID:52b4d8939c55600f821168592f0cdb4e]] I received this bag directly from the manufacturer at no cost for evaluation, and here are my thoughts.

This is a very spacious and sturdy weekend bag constructed of rugged canvas that is well complimented by dark brown crazy horse leather trim. It's 22.5" x 14" size make it acceptable as a carry on by most airlines, and it's roomy enough to fit enough for a long weekend or a trip of about five days. We own several bags just like this, and I can tell you from experience that the biggest problem with this bag isn't what it can fit, it's making sure you don't pack too much and go over the airline's weight limit.

This bag looks really great, and it's built to last. Every seam is double stitched, and attachments, handles, straps and zippers are leather reinforced, then both stitched and riveted for extra strength. The bottom of the bag has metal feet to protect the bag from scuffs, and the leather band that runs along the bottom edge protects it from scrapes and bumps when being manhandled by baggage handlers.

It's got nicely rounded handles that are comfortable to carry, and the attachment for the handles are leather reinforced and double riveted for strength. The buckles on the handle attachment straps adjust enough to secure a jacket or travel umbrella along the side of the bag too. In addition to the handles, the bag has a detachable shoulder strap that adjusts long enough to carry the bag over a shoulder or cross body. It doesn't have any padded piece for your shoulder, but the strap wide enough to bear weight without digging into your shoulder.

This is a top loading bag with a wide 22.5" top zipper which makes it easy to pack, and it has two zipper pulls which can be brought together in the center and locked with a TSA approved lock so you can protect the contents of your bag whether traveling or using it at the gym. The zipper is heavy duty and functions smoothly, giving you a nice wide opening to the bag's interior for packing and unpacking. The zipper is both stitched in place as well as reinforced with leather, and the leather zipper pulls are sewn as well as riveted for strength and durability.

Most of the bag's storage capacity is within the main compartment, but it also has a zippered vertical compartment on one side that's large enough to hold car keys and other small items, and a larger zippered compartment on the other side that's a perfect place to store your boarding passes, wallet, ID, and passport for quick access.

The inside of the bag is fully lined in a dark brown cotton material, and it's mostly open storage, with two open pouches for cell phone and other gadget on one wall, and two long zippered pockets with a long open pocket between them on the other wall. I encourage you to watch my video to see how much stuff this bag can actually hold. I think you'll find it more than spacious enough for short trips.

Canvas is a very durable material that holds up to the rigors of travel very well, so this bag should last a long time. It also sheds water pretty well, which helps keep contents dry between parking lot and terminal, but you can always scotchgard it as well if you want to give it some extra protection. Be sure to let the bag air out to dry completely if the inside gets wet. As I already mentioned, we have several bags just like this one and we absolutely love them. This bag is rugged, well made, and holds a heck of a lot.
text_fidelity_b: ECOSUSI Vintage Canvas Sport Tote Gym Bag Overnight Shoulder Bag Weekend Travel Duffel Bag Khaki

text_fidelity_a: Olive Drab Survival/Camping Canvas Water Bucket - Two (2) Gallons Carrier by Fox Outdoor Canvas water buckets.  I do not anticipate that these newer canvas buckets will perform as well as the 2 "US"  WW2 or Korean War Surplus bags I have used on and off for most of my life (yearly x 30+ years of camping and hunting). The material is a bit thinner or lighter... but still stout enough to not easily tear.  The first filling with water to the brim I lost almost the entire bucket through side seam in about an hour.  The second filling slowed down but it took 8+ gallons (and a few hours) for the canvas to swell up and stop oozing. Great as a carrier if you don't mind getting wet. Not so good for storage of liquids unless given time to swell up.  Perfect on a boat for extra anchor line or line for pots,etc....  You can rinse the salt water out and they will dry out fairly quickly without molding the line.  Price is excellent. I would purchase again as I am a believer in the amazing versatility and compact nature of the canvas bucket... buy 2... keep one in every vehicle

text_fidelity_a:
JOROTO X2 Stationary Exercise Bike | X2PRO Bluetooth Magnetic Belt Drive Indoor Cycling Bike, 300 Pounds Loads Fitness Cycle Bikes The UPS deliveryman carried this box to the front door with ease, but I quickly learned that a 108 lb., smooth, cardboard box is NOT that easy to maneuver. So just be aware this is a heavy shipment!

I was worried this was going to be a cheap and flimsy bike, but that's not the case in any way! This thing is welded, heavy gauge steel with a thick paint job (probably not powder coated). The handles are equally solid with a thick rubber grip, probably hot dipped. Basically, no amount of sweaty hands are going to cause the grip to deteriorate. The mechanics are practically silent.

Assembly is a cinch. There are 4 bolts used to attach the feet, three adjustable handles to attach the seat and handle, and two pedals to screw on. All of the required tools are in the box.

I've only ridden on it once, but the seat is soft (not that it matters if you're standing). The electronic display is of utmost cheapness, though. I was afraid that I was going to break it when installing the (included) AA batteries. It provides very basic information such as time, distance, "speed", and "calories" but there is no input for height and weight.

I'm waiting on a cadence sensor that will attach to one of the crank arms, and plan to use that with an app to get better feedback on pace. I also downloaded the Peloton app (30 day free trial) and was able to follow along just fine with the beginners ride. The resistance knob doesn't have a numeric scale (just +/-) so you'll have to judge for yourself based on how it feels.

Final thought is regarding the maneuverability. The front wheels are a bit small and made of a hard plastic so it will be hard to roll across carpet. You can tell from the photo we have a hard floor, and if it gets caught on debris, it may easily get stuck or scratch the floor.

Overall, I'm impressed with the build quality, assembly and performance. Only negatives are the ultra cheap display, lack of any integrated wireless technology (BYO), and the small wheels to move it around.
text_fidelity_b: JOROTO X2 Stationary Exercise Bike | X2PRO Bluetooth Magnetic Belt Drive Indoor Cycling Bike, 300 Pounds Loads Fitness Cycle Bikes

text_fidelity_a:
Eco Vessel Summit Discontinued 2014 Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Flip Straw (17-Ounce, Blue Glow) I really loved these bottles at first, so much so that I bought 8 of them. They keep my water very cold for a long, long time and I like the lids (I use them without the straws). I can hook them onto whatever I need to help me carry them, as well.

Unfortunately, my love affair with these bottles has ended all too soon. The first thing I noticed is that the paint started coming off. The red one is the worst. The paint is flaking off to the point that it would be better off if I pull the rest of it off to turn it silver instead of blotched red. But I could have lived with that.

What got me was when I started to fill one up only to discover that the plastic ring around the top of the bottle that you use to screw the lid in has split. It split completely down. There was nothing I could do. It had to either go back to the manufacturer or the trash. Since I'm a grad student, the last thing I have is extra time so I put it in the trash.

I started checking my other bottles and discovered that the plastic ring was put on at a tilt on some of the bottles (based on the amount of space under the ring not being uniform on all bottles).

Then I looked at my other bottles and noticed that the Hydro Flask's ring was metal, not plastic. I like those bottles just as much, but had to buy the straw lids separately. However, now that I see the flaw in the Eco Vessel bottles, I'm going to start replacing them with the Hydro Flask brand. Not only are they completely metal (except the lid, of course), but the finish does not show signs that it will flake off.

All in all, the plastic ring used to screw the lid onto the bottle is a fatal flaw for these bottles.

UPDATE: I added pictures showing the paint flaking off and the warped plastic at the top. I did not take pictures of the one that broke, but I thought showing one that's not broken yet, but clearly warped, might be helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Eco Vessel Summit Discontinued 2014 Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Flip Straw (17-Ounce, Blue Glow)

The poles are the nice coated metal type that shouldn't rust if you keep them from getting too scratched up, and they have easy set up holes for setting the net height, BUT the holes are only at 36" and 61". It would have been easy to add a few more options.

The other complaint is that the plastic bases cannot fit in the long carry bag with the poles - the opening is slightly too small. This also seems like it would have been an easy fix. That said, it's still easy to break down and store away, having just a bag for the four poles, a bag for the racquets and balls/birdies, and two handled bases that one can keep full of sand or empty of water with each use (sand is recommended, but concrete mix will work as well) and stack on top of each other. They also have caps for the filling holes.

The included racquets are the painted plywood with attached handles type that you might get with a table tennis set, only larger. They're fine, and it doesn't make much sense to include something more expensive, because if you want something more expensive you probably want to pick it out to your specifications.

Overall I like it pretty much. It doesn't take much time to set up or take down so that shouldn't stop people from playing if they so desire. It doesn't take much room to store, either, so it won't be a problem to keep in a basement or garage without getting in the way.

Gaiam Balance Ball Beginner Kit (Small, Purple) Your first observation might be similar to mine. The outdoor setting is calming and just gorgeous. The colors in this video are beautiful and the river creates a calm, quiet and peaceful setting for your workout.

I enjoyed the workout, but didn't realize how many muscles you needed to perch yourself atop a balance ball. You start off just rolling over the ball and then progress to some pretty tough balancing acts. There are some stretches which will stretch out your spine in new ways. I realized I'm not as flexible as I thought I was.

I'd advise watching this video at least once before proceeding because it is kinda difficult to follow the workout while attempting to focus on not hurtling towards the floor if you are not totally focused on what you are doing.

The kit includes:

Medium inflatable exercise ball (green, 26"/65cm)
Full-length workout video (35 minutes)
Air pump

The Air pump is "ok," but I found that an electric pump was much more efficient. If you use the air pump, you might want to do that "workout" the day before. The instruction scare you into worrying about inflating the ball too much, but never fear, with that pump, it might be impossible.

The medium exercise ball is "ok" but had I realized there was a larger balance ball, I'd have ordered the larger one since I'm taller. If you are 5' 9" and above, I'd say go for the blue balance ball (large size). I think weight also counts. If you are above your recommended weight (ideal weight and all that), then you might want a larger size.

On the side of the box it says:

Small Purple Balance Ball - Height 5' 0" to 5' 5" - Ball Size 22"/55cm
Medium Green Balance Ball - Height 5' 6 to 5' 11" - Ball Size 26"/65cm
Large Blue Balance Ball - Height 6' 0" to 6' 3" - Ball Size 30"/75cm

The exercise video is combination of shorter segments from three balance ball workouts. You really have to concentrate on making smooth and steady movements.

The way I found this workout to be most effective was to place the ball on top of a yoga mat. This prevents slippage of the ball on a carpet and also prevents you from getting injured because the yoga mat provides an additional level of protection from your hands and feet slipping on a carpet.

You will be doing three workouts.

Upper Body
Abs
Lower Body

There are times when you are either sitting, leaning over the ball or on your back, balancing and stretching out your spine. The hardest part of this workout is when you are on you back and you are rolling on top the ball. It is easier once you make full use of your powers of concentration.

The video is a nice introduction, but is really only an introduction. While you can get a good beginner's workout, I'd imagine it is more effective to order the three additional videos they recommend. Karen Voight also has a DVD out called BLT (Butt, Legs & Tummy) on a ball.

This workout will take you to new levels of concentration and mind-body awareness. It will work the upper body, lower body and abs. You will be strengthening, toning and conditioning smaller core muscles.

The 45 minutes includes a 5-minute warm-up to learn proper positioning.

If you enjoy this workout, look for:

BalanceBall Fitness Upper Body Workout
BalanceBall Fitness Abs Workout
BalanceBall Fitness Lower Body Workout

~The Rebecca Review
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Balance Ball Beginner Kit (Small, Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
Genuine Fred Howligans Dog Bandana, Large, Red I was excited to order these bandanas for my adult Corgi, Skip, and my new puppy I'm picking up soon! I got the red and the navy blue and even though there is no option to choose the size you want, based on other reviews, I was expecting the red to arrive in size small and this navy blue to be size medium/large. That is not the case. The blue one arrived first, in size small and unfortunately is too small for Skip. I can get the collar on him, but the ends barely overlap, leaving just enough space for the velcro to catch and the front triangle of material is laughably small on him.

I love the adorable print! There's images of squirrels, fire hydrants, balls, steaks and paw prints and cute sayings.. "Quite Fetching", "Ain't Too Proud To Beg". "Smell Ya later", You Gonna Eat That?", I'm All Ears!", "Gotta Run!", "Yo Dawg!" and "Shake On It". The product description claims that "the pattern is printed in reflective ink". I did not find this to be the case. The ink is silver and while it is shiny and kind of metallic, reflective it is not. This is not a deterrent for me, but may be for others.

I do like the velcro closure! I usually steer clear of dog bandanas because I don't like having to tie them on which makes the dog look silly with the two ends sticking out.. and I have rarely had luck finding a bandana that's the right size to my dog. I usually end up with a too large bandana (Corgi's a small-ish) that I fold in half into the standard triangle, tie it around his neck and then, not only does he have those "wings" sticking out from the tie, but he also is dwarfed by the size of the triangle in the front. My dogs don't need a bib or a necktie. LOL!

The sizing on this navy blue bandana (I have yet to receive the red one and am now quite curious to see what size shows up) is perfect for a smaller dog. I planned on Skip wearing this navy blue one, but it seems it will be given to my new Corgi puppy. The size small that I received will fit him properly and look right. I can only hope that I receive the red in a size medium/large so Skip gets to wear one too. If not, then the new pup will be off to a great start in the wardrobe department!

Bottom line... These are quite cute, very well made, the velcro is strong enough to hold through a round of scratching and seems as though it would hold during light play (we'll put that to the real test when our new puppy arrives!) and the size of the bandana itself (referring to the navy blue only) seems correct. But not being able to select the size you will receive is just shocking. It almost feels like a shot in the dark to order this - what size will I receive this time? That is not how anyone likes to shop and I'm surprised there is no size selection available for this reason.
text_fidelity_b: Genuine Fred Howligans Dog Bandana, Large, Red

This towel is 24" x 68" and fits my mat perfectly (as you'll see in the picture I'm going to attach). It's almost nearly perfectly non-slip, but it does move a bit during very active movements. Then again I've never owned a yoga towel yet that hasn't slipped a little, and to be completely fair, this one slipped very little. It mostly clung to my mat and gave my hands & feet all the traction I needed, so that's what I was looking for and I'm happy.

It's very well made, super soft, and the trim is well stitched so I think it's going to last a nice long time. It soaks up sweat from my hands which really helps me maintain my position much better than before, and it's nice to have it between me and my mat too! I used it to wipe down after session and it dried me off and still felt like it could absorb more if it had to. Another good feature about this towel is that it's machine washable in cold water on easy cycle and you can either air dry it (it dries fast) or tumble dry on low setting. Complete care instructions come on the packaging, so I'll not bore you with them here except to say that this yoga towel is easy to keep clean and sanitary, and having the towel keeps the yoga mat that way too.

It seems well made, durable, easy to care for, soft to the touch, grips the mat well, and is able to absorb moisture very well. It did have a slight amount of movement during vigorous movements, but not a marked amount, and it performed as it claimed to. Price seems reasonable for the quality as well in my opinion. I think it performs well and would last a long time. Five stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Burgundy I just received the Fitbit One yesterday, so I can't really give as detailed a report as some of the others I've read. I spent a very long time deciding which item to purchase - did I want a Flex? Did I want my heart rate monitored? I think the first thing to figure out is what you exactly want to accomplish.

For my needs, tracking my steps, calories burned and sleep is really what I wanted and the Fitbit One had outstanding ratings. As well, I did not want to have to wear anything on my wrist during the day. The clip vs. band was a huge plus for me. Plus the burgundy color is really nice (though where I clip it, no one sees it anyway).

I downloaded the free Fitbit app and created an account online as soon as I got it (you have to activate and set up online anyway). It asks for your goals as far as weight loss, in what time frame, steps per day goals, etc. You can make changes if you need to. Based on the goals you set for your weight loss amount and how hard you are willing to work for it (from easy at 0.5 lbs/week to very hard at 2 lbs/week), it will calculate how many calories a day you should be eating and then tell you how long it should take to reach your goal. This is the website or app, not the Fitbit One itself.

The Fitbit is small and I barely notice I'm wearing it. The clip is a rubbery material that is very soft, so it is easy to get the One into and out of the clip when you want to put it into the band for sleeping. I clip it to clothes on my upper body as per the instruction recommendations, and I don't remember it is there. You can set a message for when you first start it up, and then you can cycle through various stats, like # steps walked, stairs climbed, miles walked, calories burned, and then it will show the time all on the display.

On the website/app, you will get more details about all the areas that are tracked. When you meet a milestone, it has a little "hooray" for you - for example today I met my steps goal.

If you want it to track your sleep, you need to put it in the sleep band. I did that last night and it is super easy to get the One out of the clip and slip it into the band. I had to keep the band fairly loose so it wouldn't be uncomfortable - it isn't the softest material - but when I fell asleep I didn't even notice I had it on. In the morning, it gave me details about my sleep pattern and how long I was actually sleeping vs. how long I was in bed, which I think is super helpful.

This is a great tool, but like any tool the responsibility is still on the individual. You have to manually enter your food in the online tracker (or in the app), and it will tell you how many calories you've eaten, how many you have left, etc. It will also tell you how many you may have left because of the amount of calories you've burned. But that is all dependent on a person taking the time to put the information in and doing so accurately. For me, that's the hardest part (I've tried food tracker apps in the past). I think once I get into the habit and make it my routine, it shouldn't be so difficult.

Synching data from the One to the computer/app is done wirelessly. I noticed it makes it to my app (via bluetooth) much more quickly than it makes it to my computer. Sometimes I have to refresh the computer several times to get it to show the right number of steps, etc. However, there is so much more information in the online dashboard than in the app, and you can get into great detail about your sleep and other things that I really do want it to synch accurately (and quickly) with my computer.

My one complaint is that I didn't realize it already came with a clip and a sleep band so I bought them separately. That might be MY mistake, though, so I didn't take any stars off for it. But if you want to buy this, unless you want to have an extra clip and band just in case, you do NOT need to buy them separately.

Overall, I'm very pleased with this choice. It was a tough decision but so far so good.

I'll update if status after I've used it for awhile.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Burgundy

text_fidelity_a:
iClimb Heavy Duty Hard Arm Camping Folding Mesh Chair with Cup Holder, Bottle Opener and Carry Bag Guys, now this is the real deal! It is far from the standard, wimpy, light weight chairs you're used to seeing set up around camp fires or out on the soccer field sidelines. I am incredibly impressed.
The metal feels incredibly strong and durable. It's a very thick and heavy frame. If a kid or klutzy adult (like myself) were to bump hard into one of the arms or legs when someone was someone was sitting in it, it could easily leave a bruise. I'm not trying to suggest this chair isn't safe, but rather trying to convey just how heavy duty this metal frame is. Plus, the material the seat is made out of is very thick too. It also looks incredibly durable and like it should last a long time. I haven't had a reason to wash this chair yet, but I see no reason why this material wouldn't be easy clean if it needed it. Oh, and it is much more comfortable to sit in than the other chairs. The sturdiness helps an awful lot.
So overall, I really do like it. But because it is so "heavy duty" it is a heavy chair! Especially when to compared to what a standard folding chair weighs. I can't say for sure, but I suspect this chair probably weighs around twice as much as the average camping chair. Which probably isn't a big deal if you're not having to carry it a very long way. But lets say I had to hike quite a ways to a camping site (with the weight of all the other gear on my back too), well then I would think twice about choosing this chair. Oh and it is taller than most too. I would say it's about six inches taller then the standard folding chair.
So overall, I defiantly think this is an impressive, well made chair. I am 5'6 and a 150 pounds, so I already fit "comfortably" in a standard camping chair. For me personally, unless I had severe back pain or some other painful condition, I don't think I personally would NEED this chair. I still really like it and would prefer to sit in it, but a chair this heavy duty wouldn't be necessity for me. My 250 lb hubby on the other hand would completely disagree. He is VERY comfortable sitting in this chair. He also probably wouldn't noticed the extra length or weight of this chair if he had to carry it folded up on his back. Hands down, he would most certainly prefer this chair over the standard type of camping chair. It really is that nice. We both would recommend it. I'm even saving this as an idea to get my own dad for next Father's day!
text_fidelity_b: iClimb Heavy Duty Hard Arm Camping Folding Mesh Chair with Cup Holder, Bottle Opener and Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a:
PackIt Freezable Utility Cooler, 18 Can, Charcoal Grey The main, cooled compartment is 10.5" x 7.5" x 7" tall. It is a family-sized cooler bag for food or beverages. The gel for cooling is in the front, bottom, and back walls of the cooler. The side walls are just canvas and do not contain gel, and I don't think the top has gel either. The cooler walls can be collapsed so the cooler is flatter and smaller when you place it in the freezer. They recommend cooling it in the freezer for 12 hours before use. There is a zippered, flat outside pocket in the front that is 8.5" wide and 5.5" tall. There is a handle on top of the of the cooler under which is a compartment that will hold things like napkins, phones, utensils, etc. The opening is 5.5" wide. There is no zipper to secure this pocket. Due to the handle being right above the opening for this area, it is not highly convenient to get things in and out. This compartment is about 2" deep and covers the entire width and length of the lid. There is also a zippered, flat outer pocket tucked away on the bottom of the bag. It has an attached pull-out bit of fabric, though I'm not sure what it's for. I'm also not sure what you'd want to place in this pocket, since it's between the ground and the bottom gel wall of the cooler and weight will be on it. The cooler also has an adjustable carry strap. The cooler interior is easy to clean up if there are spills. It seems to be working okay to keep food cool for a few hours while traveling.

This cooler contains polyethylene foam. The advertising says that the "cooler is made from nontoxic poly canvas and has a food-safe, water-resistant lining" and it is made from "...PVC-, BPA-, phthalate-, formaldehyde- and lead-free materials."
text_fidelity_b: PackIt Freezable Utility Cooler, 18 Can, Charcoal Grey

text_fidelity_a:
Igloo BMX 52 Quart Cooler with Cool Riser Technology I purchased the Igloo BMX Cooler to replace an Ozark Trail 25qt rotomolded cooler that I purchased from Wal-Mart before an impromptu camping trip. I was very disappointed with the OT cooler, it claimed to hold ice for 4.5 days but on day two of my trip over half the ice was melted. I had a family member coming out to visit and camp with me so I decided to order the 52qt version of the Igloo BMX. It was actually cheaper than the Wal-Mart cooler and twice the size.

We filled the Igloo up on a Sunday afternoon packed pretty full with food, beer and water. We were planning on a 3-day trip. I saved as much ice as I could at home and we bought one more bag on the way out of town. Day 1 after over 24 hours I opened the drain and only a tiny bit of water came out. Already much better performance. On Tuesday we moved campsites and got gas and added another bag of ice since we bought more food to replenish. Day 3 on Wednesday a fair amount of water drained from the cooler but it still had plenty of ice and was plenty cold. I had put 8 frozen water bottles inside and they were all frozen still.

I went to empty the cooler on Day 4, a full ~96 hours of use and there was still a lot of ice left in it. I have no doubt that you could make this last 5 days or even longer if you keep adding fresh ice every couple of days. If we didn't add the second bag, most of it would have probably melted by day 3/4.

At the time of this review I purchased the red/black 52qt cooler for $77. I'm impressed enough with it that I decided to order a 25qt one was well for solo trips and returned my Ozark Trail cooler. I will add another review or update this one after I use the 25qt cooler. But $140 for a nice rotomolded 52qt and 25qt cooler is less than half the price of ONE comparable Yeti. So glad I didn't buy into the hype.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo BMX 52 Quart Cooler with Cool Riser Technology

Minuses:

Timex Unisex The Timex Ironman run Trainer 2.0 GPS watch is a very good gps watch for runners and probably swimmers, too. I don't swim, so couldn't test that part. Despite the name "Ironman" this watch is designed for running and "approved" for swimming (that's from the Timex website where they cite "water resistant approved for 50 meters"). When I think of Ironman, I think of the big three: running, biking, and swimming. So don't let the name fool you into thinking this will connect to your bike sensors as well. That being said, if you are looking for a good watch with a heart rate monitor, this is a decent choice.

I used the watch with my existing ANT+ heart rate monitor and foot pod (both are Garmin devices). The watch synched perfectly with both. If you use a foot pod it can (and should) be calibrated so that you can then accurately track your distance and pace when you're forced to run indoors on a treadmill. The display is clean, easy to read and customizable. I also have small wrists, so was a little concerned about fit, but the watch fit comfortably on me while wearing. It is smaller and a bit more comfortable than the Garmin 310xt (the only other GPS watch I own, so compared it to that). You can even set reminders for when you need to hydrate or fuel up during a long run. Plus you can also create intervals to do interval training.

The thing I dont like about the watch is that I can't also use it for biking like I can with my [[ASIN:B0025VKUPM Garmin Forerunner 310XT]]. Which seems contrary to the fact that not only do they call it "ironman" but it even has the word "triathalon" on the watch face. however, that being said, you can use it for swimming, as I previously mentioned, as it supposedly is water resistant up to 50 meters. I am not a swimmer, so didn't try that, but I am a cyclist (as I already mentioned -- I guess I'm getting redundant here).

The GPS accuracy on the watch is pretty good. It appears to be a little more accurate than my Garmin 310xt, but the difference to me is negligible, especially if I set my Garmin to capture data every second rather than have it on "auto" - then the resulting map traces are almost identical.

Another feature that I'm not too keen on is the way you view the data. They have you use their web-based system, which I found to be too "bulky" - it has too many options and too confusing. Many of the options are only available if you pay for their premium plan. You can't even export the data into a GPX or TCX file without having paid. this is something that pretty much every other company allows for free. I did find a way around that, though. With the watch connected to your computer via the USB port, it becomes just like another USB drive on your machine and you can navigate to the folder that has your activities stored in it. Timex uses the FIT format. Luckily, Strava (a great app and website for tracking cycling and running), will import these files. Just drag the FIT file to your computer somewhere and import it into Strava. It takes a few minutes for Strava to get process the file after it imports, so if all your run information is not showing up right away, wait a few minutes and then refresh or go back to it and you should see it. Then Strava will let you export it to a GPX format which then can be imported into Runkeeper or many other popular fitness apps. Kind of some extra steps, but if you stick with this and Strava, you'll be set. Strava also has a premium (paid) feature, but I only have their basic (free) account and can do everything I need with it.

Overall, this is a really nice watch, and hopefully they will come up with a "lighter" version of their software, but for now, I am not even going to mess with it and stick with Strava.
text_fidelity_b: Timex Unisex

text_fidelity_a:
Withings ActivitÃ Steel - Activity and Sleep Tracking Watch I had high hopes for this device. I think it's aimed at people who don't want a gadget to play with, but a useful and attractive minimalist activity tracker. It qualifies as attractive and, if all you want to do is count steps, it is useful. Ultimately, I had to quit wearing it because it caused a severe rash on my wrist under one side of the band. I have reached out to Withings and I will update this review when my issue is resolved (or not). At this point I just want to return it for the following reasons:

1. The rash was severe. I've now gone 2 weeks without wearing the watch and it has barely diminished. I'm not allergic to silicone, so I wonder what chemicals are in or on the band.
2. The lack of contrast between the hands and the face result in a watch I can only read in good light. In a dimly lit room it is completely unreadable.
3. A big reason the watch appealed to me is that I can wear it while swimming. It is supposed to log swim time, but it was unreliable to the point of being useless for this purpose.
4. I was intrigued by the sleep tracking, but it has quirks that make me doubt it's usefulness. For example, if I sit on the couch reading or watching TV for an hour before bed, sometimes it logs this as sleep, including deep sleep.

The watch counts from 50% to 20% less steps than my Samsung app. I can't say which is more accurate. I like the idea of an elegant and simple tracker/watch, and this was almost it. Ultimately nothing else matters because I can't wear it. The negatives add up to the point that I'm not interested in resolving the rash problem with a different band.

Update: I reached out to Withings. They responded quickly and seemed genuinely concerned. They dealt with my problem promptly and fairly. I'm upping my review from 2 stars to 3 stars because of the customer service.
text_fidelity_b: Withings ActivitÃ Steel - Activity and Sleep Tracking Watch

text_fidelity_a:
ACCUSPLIT Survivor II - S2XL Stopwatch, Clock I use a stopwatch a lot to time my exercise. This is the best stopwatch I've ever owned in this price range. It's sturdily made in a color I love, deep red (the company that makes it offers a great selection of colors). The design itself is quite attractive, with a pleasant oval shape, large numbers which are easy to read, and a good grade of plastic. Best of all, the action of the function keys is very smooth. The keys on the last few stopwatches I owned had a rough action, and for the most recent one, that's what caused it to die. The left, top function key got stuck and couldn't be unjammed.

One downside--which seems to be consistent across all stopwatches I've owned--is that the instructions are hard to read. They are in small type, confusing and incomplete. However, my husband and I together were able to figure out something I never could with my last stopwatch, how to turn off the hourly chime. That drove me crazy with the other one because the clock on it ran fast so it never did chime on the hour. It was too much trouble to keep resetting the clock because I never used it since I wear a watch.

Tip for turning off the alarm which is not in the instructions: Follow the instructions to get to the alarm. Hold down the (R) right button and tap once on the (L) left button. You will see the alarm symbol go away. Tap it again to make it come back. If you set the alarm, frankly, I have no idea how to turn it off when it rings but this. If you tap on the (R) button once, it acts like a snooze alarm, and the alarm rings again in about sixty seconds.

I give this product high marks for the uses I mentioned.
text_fidelity_b: ACCUSPLIT Survivor II - S2XL Stopwatch, Clock

text_fidelity_a:
Kohree Portable Butane Gas Stove for Outdoor Cooking, 10,000BTU Camping Burner Stove with Dual Wind-Guard, Butane Single Gas Burner Backpacking with Carry Case for Travel, Hiking Trip, Home Emergency We have a small shed that we use in the winter to get away when snow has us limited, or in the other times of year to just get a fresh perspective on life. In the winter, we often will use our wood stove to get some water heated or make simple breakfasts. Having another little burner sounded like a good idea.

HOW WE INTEND TO USE THIS
We are using this in a shed on a stable table top. We are not taking this camping, so it will be in a protected area and not dragged around a lot.

STURDY?
For dragging this around- it is okay, but kind of flimsy. I would suggest a crate or box to protect it or wrap of some sort when camping and transporting.

CANISTER
I gave my husband specific instructions to get BUTANE canisters for this stove. He was doing the "I know, I am not stupid" routine despite me saying he HAD to be sure and he was annoyed at me for insinuating that he would ever not know the difference between anything in a hardware store.

He came home with Propane in canisters. Be sure to pay attention to the canisters you are buying. Do not get the refill canisters that you use to fill lighters with and do not get propane, even if it DOES look like a cheaper deal. *rolls eyes at husband*

WIND GUARD
The wind guard is flimsy. If you are planning to use this outside, it is not going to protect you terribly well from wind. It helps a little, but is not that stable.

PERFORMANCE
Once I got the right canisters we were able to take the stove for a run. It is a great little stove for a single pan meal or tea/coffee water. It heats quickly and as long as you don't have a huge heavy pan on it, it will stay well and be stable.

SURFACE
We have this on a solid table top. Plan on having a solid surface to stand this on as well. It is pretty lightweight, so you will want to guard against sliding and shifting around.

PORTABILITY
This is easy to transport, small enough to carry, and is not too heavy. It also tends to be not quite as sturdy as it could be.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice little burner for emergencies. It works great in our shed, but outdoors, you need to be sure to have a stable surface that does not slide easily to put this on. It works well, but in wind, it might give you issues. Just be sure to get the right canisters before planning on using this.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I wish it was a little bit sturdier and did not slide around as much on the surface as it does. Otherwise it is a pretty decent little burner for emergencies and get-aways.
text_fidelity_b: Kohree Portable Butane Gas Stove for Outdoor Cooking, 10,000BTU Camping Burner Stove with Dual Wind-Guard, Butane Single Gas Burner Backpacking with Carry Case for Travel, Hiking Trip, Home Emergency

text_fidelity_a: Dart World Piranha Razor Grip 90% Tungsten Dart (24-Gram) I'm relatively newish to darts.  I've played off and on for years but still considered myself new now that I'm practicing and playing on a regular basis.  I had been playing with borrowed darts and wanted a quality set without breaking the bank and that's just what I've got in this set.  These darts feel fantastic off the fingers and they fly so much more true than my original set.  I've had fewer bounce outs with these darts.  I was skeptical of the spinning shaft.  Quite honestly the spinning portion of the shaft is made out of pretty cheap plastic but I've come to appreciate them even though I've had to replace one shaft due to a direct hit which broke the plastic.  Replacements are easily found and relatively inexpensive.  I have to agree with a previous reviewer that the spinning shaft does extend the life of the flights by spinning out when hit by another dart.  The bottom line is that you can't go wrong with these darts...they're a great bargain.  What I've learned is that while you DO want a quality dart...a higher priced dart isn't necessarily better...a quality darter thrower with a lesser set of darts will always beat a less skilled thower with a high priced set.  Find the set that suits you as a thrower...what set anyone decides to stick with is a very personal thing.

text_fidelity_a:
WLOOD Golf Cart Speaker Mount, Universal Portable Adjustable Strap Fits Most Bluetooth Wireless Speakers Attachment Accessory Holder Bar Rail Who wouldn’t love some great tunes on their golf cart..?!! As a family who owns a golf cart yet, has never golfed a day in our life - we’ve spent the last decade doing nothing but, fun rides and adventures all around our planned community with our kiddos on this toy. Music would only enhance this- and give us golf cart karaoke?!!

Problem is.. this is a one size fits most. But, it didn’t come close to being “most” for us! How.. when we have the same speaker used in the sellers sample photo description- see photo I included..??!! Right from start when trying to attach we had issues.. this has 6 velcro straps coming out of the sides- (picture a big bug with legs!) Zero instructions included and you'd think this would be straightforward.. Trust me, we tried straps forward wrapping around pole and then, backwards just the same- we even went back to description online.. studied the photo and still had no success.

Problems we incurred:

•Straps are not long enough to wrap around the pole and speaker- and have enough length to close on themself. (this is placing the speaker in same spot as advertised!)

•2 of the 3 sets of straps were sewn in backwards- so, if wrapping around the direction they’re attached- The Velcro teeth on x2 straps are on the wrong side. (Equivalent to getting two negative signs together..) hoping this is an error!

•From photo description it appears we are missing a middle extra strap? Photo shows x1 in brown strap thru middle but, we don’t have anything of the sort...??

•This has no bottom support or “shelf” for added protection.. this could lead speaker slide at the bottom if it were to become a loose. Golf carts bounce around a bit and vibration may cause this to slip. So, bottom support would be helpful if not, necessary to protect the speaker from falling down and give the user peace of mind.

•This is missing a simple but straightforward set of instructions.

overall, this may work with a much smaller size speaker- one with hardly any girth.. Even then, it may be hit/miss to get the securely fastened. I’m afraid a smaller speaker may not produce enough sound to be heard over a motorized golf cart and will it stay safe? In leui of listing this “one size fits all/most..” this would be beneficial to list the actual length and dimension of straps so, one can verify speaker sizes that would work! Listed at a price point of $10- this could be a great find.. if, it could be successful. Tbh, It may be safer to invest more solid option to ensure it will fit/function as expected. I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: WLOOD Golf Cart Speaker Mount, Universal Portable Adjustable Strap Fits Most Bluetooth Wireless Speakers Attachment Accessory Holder Bar Rail

Arc Flashlight and Lighter Just came back from a camping trip and this looked like a great idea so I was really looking forward to it getting here. Unfortunately I have been underwhelmed. Much smaller and less solid that I expected. And not waterproof at all. I have other flashlights in the same size range and they feel much more sturdy. The beam of the flash light is pretty weak and diffused. A small bright spot in the middle and thin weak circle surrounding it. Not really useful at all beyond 5 or 6 feet. The lens cover is a very thin plastic and likely to be very easily scratched or broken. There is no water seal around the lens. On the other end you have the arc lighter. While works well, it is too small to be any more useful that lighting a cigarette. If you wanted to use it camping you have use it to light a piece of paper and then use the paper to light something else. The USB charging port is under the cap that covers the Arc lighter. This cap is not waterproof and the minute you get this area wet the whole thing is ruined.
Given that it is clearly not designed to be used as a camping tool (which is exactly what comes to mind when looking at the listing.) I am not sure where it fits. Maybe if you are a smoker that has to walk outside to smoke? This is an interesting concept that was poorly executed.

Unfortunately this is a 'Not Recommend'. Wouldn't spend my own money on it.

Aerobie Superdisc (6044022) My Black Lab can't get enough Frisbee, she demands it at least twice a day. Unlike the flying discs made specifically for dogs, these fly just like a real Frisbee (both in distance and flight pattern) yet have the soft rim so the dog"s mouth isn't injured when she catches it in mid-air. The brightly colored rim makes them easy to find when my throwing gets too wild and they end up somewhere she can't get to. The rim is squared off and ever so slightly raised above the actual disc which makes it easier for her to pick up if it lands flat on a slick or level surface.

I have tried many versions of Frisbees through the last 40 years of Labs in my life and these are by far the best. The one I just had to throw out was over 5 years old and eventually cracked in half but up until then flew perfectly despite being riddled with teeth marks, dents, and small cracks.

The size makes them unsuitable for small dogs (obviously) and because the rim is the only color they may be difficult for dogs (and humans) with imperfect eyesight to see.

GTGlobal Multifunctional Beach Blanket/ Picnic Mat with Carrying Pouch 7 X 5 Feet, Waterproof Tarp, Extra Large Perfect for Beach Party/ Outdoors/ Camping/ Hiking - Green Measuring 7'x5', the GT Global Beach Blanket is a nice size for a picnic lunch or to spread out on the beach for sunbathing. As others have previously noted, this "blanket" is a lightweight, thin, smooth nylon-like material with grommets around the sides, so it's more of a light tarp rather than a blanket, but that's not at all bad. This material stays cool to the touch so it would be a real relief to sunbathe on this rather than my towel which transfers heat directly to me when laying on it.

Sand doesn't stick to this material and water beads up and rolls right off it, so you could use this as a protective layer to keep your beach towels or blanket clean. Being very light, it's easy for the breeze to catch it and sail it away, so it has grommets strategically positioned around the sides which would allow it to be staked down. (Stakes not included). It could also make a handy sunshade if you had someplace to secure it from and some line.

It comes in a nylon carry case that's very tight so it's a bit of an effort to remove it. When you're done using it the bag would be handy to store it in again, but it's so tight that I was unable to place it back in. The manufacturer really needs to make the carry bag large enough that people could use it without struggling.

Even without going back into the bag though, this tarp folds and rolls up into a small bundle that would be easy to take along to the beach, waterpark, on camping trips, to stick in a backpack for trekking, or to stow on a boat. Besides using it for picnics or at the beach, this tarp would be very useful to have along when camping to provide a dry place to sit or to cover food stores or gear. Backpackers would find it useful to provide a safe dry seating area, to hang up by the grommets to get out of sudden downpours, and even as something to sleep on at night in a pinch. Boaters could find this tarp useful in many of the same ways and more, so this tarp has uses that go way beyond "beach blanket", and for those reasons I like it.

I'm giving it four stars rather than five because it's impossible to return the tarp to the carry bag once it's out of it, and it needs to come with stakes to hold it down in sand to be ready to use. Promotional discount received for evaluation and review purposes.
text_fidelity_b: GTGlobal Multifunctional Beach Blanket/ Picnic Mat with Carrying Pouch 7 X 5 Feet, Waterproof Tarp, Extra Large Perfect for Beach Party/ Outdoors/ Camping/ Hiking - Green

TETON Sports Celsius XXL Sleeping Bag; Great for Family Camping; Free Compression Sack After decades of backpacking with mummy sleeping bags, and never having enough warmth, we transitioned to 4WD tent camping. Although I never really minded the confines of a mummy bag my wife was never crazy about it so we looked for a bag with lots of space, width, and warmth. Weight and bag compression was no longer the primary criteria for purchasing a sleeping bag. That's good because this baby is relatively heavy and doesn't exactly pack small once taken out of the box, but that's fine for 4WD camping.

Experience has taught me that you want to purchase a sleeping bag that is rated at least 20 to 30 degrees colder than the coldest temperatures you expect to encounter. We occasionally camp in the mountains where night time temps drop into the high 20's and low 30's, but most of the time the night time temps are in the 40s to low 70s in a relatively dry Western-US environment, including the high desert. I was concerned we might overheat but my wife and I have remained comfortable across the entire temperature range wearing just a t-shirt and underwear or long underwear. She zips her bag up completely whenever the temps drop into the 40s or lower. I don't think I've zipped mine up completely yet.

We're no longer sleeping on a thin foam pad on the ground. We use these bags on cots with 3" thick foam pads. We both sleep like a rock. Our mummy bags have been handed down to our grown kids. As sleeping bags go, this one is a winner!
text_fidelity_b: TETON Sports Celsius XXL Sleeping Bag; Great for Family Camping; Free Compression Sack

text_fidelity_a:
Lowepro Photo Hatchback 22L AW. Outdoor Day Camera Backpack for DSLR and Mirrorless Cameras As a 4'11" woman I didn't want too large a bag, but this is a little too small for anything other than a day bag. I could fit one medium to long lens (I squeezed in a Nikor 70-300) and a medium DSLR (I have a Nikon D5200) tightly in the camera compartment. I like the removable camera "case", which you can use to protect a camera in another bag. It will be a good commuting bag, but too small for a trip. I could fit my iPad in with the Logitech Ultrathin keyboard cover, and by opening the velcro inside slip the 15" MacBook Air inside behind the camera holder if needed. The camera access next to the body is a security feature, but be careful not to drop the lens or camera out when moving the case (I hate to admit the lens popped out while sliding the case horizontally on a bench). There is sufficient room in the top compartment for lunch or whatever you need, and I was able to tuck my small travel tripod into the side holder. Still need a travel bag.

Update: Took this on a trip to Peru in June, 2014, and used this bag for a mirrorless camera with three lenses, with plenty of room for charger, extra batteries, lens cleaner, etc. Was able to stuff my rain jacket in the top, carry a water bottle, iPad, and monopod in the side pocket hooked to the bag with the carabiner, so it stayed in place. Worked very well with smaller cameras, even on the airplane. Raising my opinion to four stars. Holding up well without showing noticeable wear and tear. Got the bigger one for the trip, but returned it, as too big for me.
text_fidelity_b: Lowepro Photo Hatchback 22L AW. Outdoor Day Camera Backpack for DSLR and Mirrorless Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
TRX Training Essentials: Flexibility DVD, Workouts to Improve Flexibility I'm very impressed with suspension strap workouts. Doing strength training, instant adjustments to resistance are possible just by adjusting by an inch or two how close you are to the anchor. And almost every strength exercise, whether for arms or legs, also involves the core. Which is amazing.

But the best thing about the straps are for stretching and flexibility. I can get deeper, longer, more supported stretches with these then with any other method I've ever tried. And my friends have called me a stretch fanatic for years.

This DVD gives detailed descriptions of 10 or 12 stretches, with progressions for each one. Their "workout" is about 45 min. long. Or you can use the "exercise library" which gives detailed descriptions of each with their progressions. Watch the exercise library for a much shorter stretch workout or pause with your remote to work an individual stretch longer.

You can probably find most of these stretches on the internet, but I'm glad I got this DVD which I got in a 3 DVD package that included a strength and cardio DVD. The strength is a pretty good workout. Haven't tried the cardio yet.

Notice I haven't mentioned TRX once yet in this review. Although I do own a TRX and like it, you can get VERY similar suspension straps on Amazon for $24.99. I got RopeInaBag and use it for travel because it is much lighter and more compact while still being plenty strong.

Regardless of the brand of straps you use, I highly recommend the stretches in this DVD.
text_fidelity_b: TRX Training Essentials: Flexibility DVD, Workouts to Improve Flexibility

text_fidelity_a:
Body Bar Power & Grace DVD This workout uses both a body bar and the gliding disks. Instructor Mindy Mylrea is joined by Keli Roberts, who modifies some of the exercises, and Violet Zaki, who increases the intensity.

Mylrea starts with a long (about 7 minutes) warm-up. During the warm-up, you are just holding the body bar and not really using it for resistance. In addition, she does not step on the disks until about halfway through the warm-up; at that time, she incorporates added moves such as twists plus side and back lunges.

For the standing portion of the workout, Mylrea takes greater advantage of the body bar. The option is often to hold the bar at the chest, on the shoulders, or overhead while performing classic strength moves such as side and front lunges, curtsey lunges, and deadlifts. The standing segment ends with push-up/plank work with the feet on the disks.

The floor work is shorter (18 minutes), but it continues to focus on the lower body with bridges and other moves targeting the hamstrings. Mylrea also includes abs work and a nice floor stretch (6 minutes), bringing in the entire workout right around 54 minutes.

I really enjoy Mylrea's original Gliding set, as I like mixing and matching from the 3 workouts on that DVD. For some reason, this workout didn't click as well with me, even though there aren't any major problems with the workout itself. One issue is that I do not have a body bar; substituting an unweighted stick and dumbbells worked okay, but this took some fun out of the workout. I also think that I have moved away from these type of cardio/strength circuit workouts now that I have discovered kettlebells.

For those who own both a body bar and gliding disks, however, I would recommend this DVD.
text_fidelity_b: Body Bar Power & Grace DVD

text_fidelity_a:
Graber Guardian 3 Bike Trunk Rack We didn't have any problem attaching this to our vehicle. It's light at only 7 lbs so didn't have any problem lifting and holding it up while securing it onto our vehicle.
Only had two bikes to attach to it on the first trip out with us using it.
We have straight bars on our bikes so have no idea if attaching a slanted bar bike on it would be any different.
Because I don't trust any holding system 100%, I always use extra straps to secure our bikes on any rack we use. Driving 70 mph, on the highway, is not the time to find out something didn't hold right or something breaking. So, always use extra caution when transporting something either on top or on the back of a moving vehicle.
Only con i have is that I do wish it had 2 stabilizing arm bars, that sit on the trunk, instead of the only 1 this model has. I think it would have the rack be more stable and less of a chance of it sliding or tilting sideways.
All in all this bike rack is nice for anyone who doesn't have a hitch on their vehicle.
